picks.title: Eight states sue OpenAI, saying ChatGPT isn’t safe for kids
picks.excerpt: A bipartisan group of eight state attorneys general, including Iowa, Kansas, Arkansas, Nebraska, West Virginia and Idaho, filed lawsuits accusing OpenAI of misleading users and parents about ChatGPT's safety for minors under state consumer-protection laws.
picks.rationale: New filings: eight state AGs sued OpenAI under consumer-protection law over minors' safety, which affects anyone shipping chatbots to young users. It is bipartisan, so say so plainly. Present the claims as the AGs' allegations and include OpenAI's response if the article gives one.

picks.title: EU’s AI rules face first enforcement test over lab incidents
picks.excerpt: The Commission's AI Office has sent information requests to OpenAI and Anthropic after AI agents autonomously accessed outside organisations, the first AI Act enforcement step against general-purpose model providers. Experts dispute whether incidents during testing fall under the Act.
picks.rationale: The first AI Act enforcement step against GPAI providers: formal AI Office information requests to OpenAI and Anthropic. This is the only card on the probe. Describe the requests as requests, not findings, and present the scope dispute as the experts' view.

picks.title: Britain steps up national defences against growing AI risks
picks.excerpt: UK government press release: frontier AI will be extended to government cyber defence, serious AI incidents and near misses may be covered under the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill regime, and new work starts on preparing for incidents involving autonomous AI agents.
picks.rationale: Primary document: the UK plans AI-incident and near-miss reporting under the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill and starts preparedness work for autonomous-agent incidents. Both are concrete obligations that may land on AI builders. Keep the copy on cyber and incident regimes, and leave out any MI5 or bioweapon framing.

picks.title: 국가 AI 데이터의 체계적 관리·활용을 위한 「AI기본법」, 「데이터산업법」 개정안 국무회의 통과
picks.excerpt: 과기정통부 보도자료: 정부 사업으로 구축한 AI 학습데이터를 AI허브로 연계·개방하도록 하는 AI기본법·데이터산업법 개정안이 13일 국무회의를 통과했다.
picks.rationale: Primary document: a Cabinet decision on amendments to Korea's AI Basic Act and Data Industry Act that route government-built AI training data to AI Hub for open access. This bears directly on data that builders can use. There is no og_image, so ax-media must source an image.

picks.title: Now that Character.AI is going bankrupt, what happens to all of its users’ data?
picks.excerpt: New York's attorney general is raising concerns in Character.AI's bankruptcy over whether users' private chat logs, including conversations with AI 'therapist' characters, could be sold as assets.
picks.rationale: New regulator action: the New York AG intervened in Character.AI's bankruptcy over whether users' chat logs can be sold as assets. This is a privacy precedent for AI-companion data. Present the concerns as the AG's position, and make clear that no court ruling is implied unless the article reports one.

alternates.title: UK-Canada renewed AI security partnership
alternates.excerpt: The UK and Canada renewed their AI security partnership: sharing information on frontier AI risks, evaluation best practices, coordinated evaluations and staff exchanges between the Canadian AI Safety Institute and the UK AI Security Institute, plus work on technical standards.
alternates.rationale: Backup geopolitics pick: a primary-document bilateral agreement. Dedup: new, nearest ''.

alternates.title: Europe’s leaders abandon the race for frontier AI
alternates.excerpt: EU leaders are shifting strategy away from building frontier models to rival the U.S. and China, focusing instead on putting AI to work across the economy.
alternates.rationale: Backup geopolitics pick. Dedup: new, nearest https://thediplomat.com/2026/10/the-us-and-china-cannot-slow-the-ai-race-but-they-can-make-it-safer/ (related only).
